drug_profiles.name: Trifluridine/tipiracil
drug_profiles.drug_class: Thymidine-based nucleoside analogue with thymidine phosphorylase inhibitor
drug_profiles.mechanism: Trifluridine is incorporated into DNA and disrupts DNA function. Tipiracil inhibits thymidine phosphorylase, increasing systemic exposure to trifluridine.

drug_profiles.name: Fluorouracil
drug_profiles.mechanism: Intracellular metabolites inhibit thymidylate synthase and can be incorporated into RNA and DNA, disrupting nucleic-acid synthesis and function.

drug_profiles.name: Folinic acid
drug_profiles.mechanism: Stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate synthase complex, enhancing fluorouracil-mediated inhibition of thymidylate synthesis. It is not itself a cytotoxic component in these regimens.

drug_profiles.name: Oxaliplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that interfere with DNA replication and transcription, leading to cell death.

drug_profiles.name: Irinotecan
drug_profiles.mechanism: Its active metabolite SN-38 stabilises the topoisomerase I–DNA complex, preventing repair of single-strand breaks during DNA replication.

drug_profiles.name: Durvalumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks its interaction with PD-1 and CD80, supporting restoration of antitumour T-cell activity.

drug_profiles.name: Pembrolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, reducing inhibitory signalling in activated T cells.

drug_profiles.name: Nivolumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-1 and blocks ligand-mediated inhibitory signalling, supporting antitumour T-cell responses.

drug_profiles.name: Atezolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds PD-L1 and blocks interactions with PD-1 and CD80, reducing checkpoint-mediated suppression of T-cell activity.

drug_profiles.name: Pemetrexed
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits folate-dependent enzymes involved in purine and thymidylate synthesis, impairing DNA and RNA synthesis.

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms platinum–DNA adducts and cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

drug_profiles.name: Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Promotes microtubule assembly and prevents normal microtubule disassembly, disrupting mitosis and intracellular transport.

drug_profiles.name: Docetaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Stabilises microtubules and inhibits their depolymerisation, causing disruption of mitotic and cellular functions.

drug_profiles.name: Doxorubicin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Intercalates into DNA, inhibits topoisomerase II and generates reactive species, causing DNA damage and impaired replication.

drug_profiles.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Delivers doxorubicin in a pegylated liposomal formulation. Released doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II.

drug_profiles.name: Cyclophosphamide
drug_profiles.mechanism: Hepatic activation produces metabolites that form DNA cross-links, interfering with DNA replication and cell division.

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds the extracellular domain of HER2, inhibiting signalling and promoting immune-mediated destruction of HER2-expressing tumour cells.

drug_profiles.name: Pertuzumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds a different extracellular HER2 domain from trastuzumab and inhibits ligand-dependent HER2 dimerisation with other HER family receptors.

drug_profiles.name: Abemaciclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, reducing retinoblastoma-protein phosphorylation and limiting progression from G1 to S phase.

drug_profiles.name: Bevacizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds VEGF-A and reduces activation of VEGF receptors, inhibiting tumour-associated angiogenic signalling.

drug_profiles.name: Gemcitabine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Active metabolites inhibit ribonucleotide reductase and are incorporated into DNA, impairing DNA synthesis.

drug_profiles.name: Cisplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Forms intra- and inter-strand DNA cross-links that disrupt DNA replication and transcription.

drug_profiles.name: Axitinib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2 and VEGFR-3 signalling, reducing angiogenesis and tumour vascular growth.

drug_profiles.name: Enfortumab vedotin
drug_profiles.drug_class: Nectin-4-directed antibody linked to a microtubule-disrupting payload
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds Nectin-4, is internalised and releases monomethyl auristatin E, which disrupts microtubules and induces cell death.

drug_profiles.name: Sacituzumab govitecan
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds Trop-2 on tumour cells and delivers SN-38, the active metabolite of irinotecan. SN-38 inhibits topoisomerase I, producing DNA damage during replication; released payload may also affect nearby tumour cells.

evidence_records.publication_title: Randomized Trial of TAS-102 for Refractory Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports trifluridine/tipiracil in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer after standard therapies.
evidence_records.limitations: Placebo-controlled later-line population. The publication supports trifluridine/tipiracil monotherapy and does not itself establish a trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact medicine, schedule family and disease setting
evidence_records.trial_population: 800 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer refractory to, or intolerant of, standard therapies.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 7.1 months versus 5.3 months; hazard ratio for death 0.68.
Median progression-free survival was 2.0 months versus 1.7 months; hazard ratio 0.48.

evidence_records.publication_title: Oxaliplatin, Fluorouracil, and Leucovorin as Adjuvant Treatment for Colon Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Adjuvant colon cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Established the clinical value of adding oxaliplatin to fluorouracil and folinic acid in adjuvant colon cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial used FOLFOX4 rather than the exact modified FOLFOX-6 schedule and does not cover every indication listed in the shared NCCP protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Regimen-family evidence; schedule differs
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending
evidence_records.trial_population: 2246 patients with completely resected stage II or III colon cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: FOLFOX4: oxaliplatin plus infusional and bolus fluorouracil with folinic acid every 2 weeks for 12 cycles.
evidence_records.comparator: LV5FU2 fluorouracil and folinic acid without oxaliplatin.
key_findings: Three-year disease-free survival was 78.2% with FOLFOX4 versus 72.9% with LV5FU2; hazard ratio 0.77.
At 10 years, overall survival was 71.7% versus 67.1% in the overall stage II/III population; the clearest overall-survival benefit was in stage III disease.

evidence_records.publication_title: Irinotecan Combined with Fluorouracil Compared with Fluorouracil Alone as First-Line Treatment for Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 387 patients with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Irinotecan combined with fluorouracil and folinic acid.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Response and time-to-progression outcomes, with overall survival assessed.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Establishes the clinical contribution of adding irinotecan to a fluorouracil/folinic-acid backbone in metastatic colorectal cancer and supports the FOLFIRI treatment concept.
key_findings: Objective response was 49% with irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid versus 31% with fluorouracil/folinic acid alone.
Median time to progression was 6.7 versus 4.4 months, and median overall survival was 17.4 versus 14.1 months.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial is backbone evidence for metastatic colorectal cancer. NCCP 00227 also lists metastatic oesophageal and second-line pancreatic indications, and the trial does not validate those settings or every detail of the current local 14-day schedule.
evidence_records.match_type: Backbone evidence for the colorectal indication

evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports modified FOLFIRINOX in the adjuvant pancreatic-cancer setting.
evidence_records.limitations: The NCCP protocol also includes metastatic treatment; this publication specifically supports the adjuvant context.

evidence_records.publication_title: Durvalumab after Chemoradiotherapy in Stage III Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent chemoradiotherapy
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports consolidation durvalumab following definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy in the studied stage III NSCLC population.
evidence_records.limitations: The PACIFIC trial used weight-based dosing every 2 weeks. The current NCCP protocol uses 1500 mg every 28 days and applies current European and local eligibility criteria, including PD-L1 requirements.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact treatment strategy and disease setting; administration schedule differs
evidence_records.trial_population: 713 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy.
evidence_records.intervention: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks for up to 12 months.
evidence_records.comparator: Placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 16.8 months versus 5.6 months; hazard ratio 0.52 in the initial analysis.
The 24-month overall-survival rate was 66.3% versus 55.6%; hazard ratio for death 0.68.
Estimated 5-year overall survival was 42.9% versus 33.4% in the updated analysis.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports pembrolizumab with pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy in the specified first-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC setting.
evidence_records.limitations: KEYNOTE-189 allowed cisplatin or carboplatin, whereas this NCCP protocol specifies carboplatin. The current NCCP schedule and eligibility criteria remain authoritative.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact immunotherapy and pemetrexed-platinum strategy; platinum selection narrowed locally
evidence_records.trial_population: 616 patients with previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without sensitising EGFR or ALK alterations.
evidence_records.intervention: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy, followed by protocol-defined maintenance treatment.
evidence_records.comparator: Placebo plus pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy.
key_findings: Estimated 12-month overall survival was 69.2% versus 49.4%; hazard ratio for death 0.49.
Median progression-free survival was 8.8 months versus 4.9 months; hazard ratio 0.52.
At 5 years, overall survival was 19.4% versus 11.3% in the updated analysis.

evidence_records.evidence_context: High-risk early triple-negative breast cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports neoadjuvant pembrolizumab with chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab in high-risk early triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The full treatment sequence, phase-specific chemotherapy details and eligibility criteria must be checked against the current NCCP protocol. Evidence outcomes apply to the complete perioperative strategy rather than an isolated phase.

evidence_records.intervention: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus platinum-containing chemotherapy, followed by surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab.
evidence_records.comparator: Matched placebo plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy, followed by surgery and adjuvant placebo.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Pathological complete response and event-free survival; overall survival was subsequently reported.
key_findings: Pathological complete response was 64.8% versus 51.2% at the first interim analysis.
Estimated 36-month event-free survival was 84.5% versus 76.8%; hazard ratio 0.63.
Estimated 60-month overall survival was 86.6% versus 81.7% in the later analysis.

evidence_records.evidence_context: Neoadjuvant HER2-positive early or locally advanced breast cancer
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Included an anthracycline-free docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab cohort relevant to TCHP.
evidence_records.limitations: The study was phase 2 and designed primarily around cardiac safety rather than a definitive comparative efficacy endpoint.

evidence_records.intervention: Three neoadjuvant pertuzumab/trastuzumab-containing cohorts; arm C received docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab for 6 cycles.
evidence_records.comparator: No conventional control arm; three active regimens were evaluated primarily for cardiac safety.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Cardiac safety, including symptomatic left-ventricular systolic dysfunction and protocol-defined LVEF decline.
key_findings: Breast pathological complete response (ypT0/is) was 66.2% in the anthracycline-free TCHP cohort.
In the TCHP cohort, 3.9% had an LVEF decline of at least 10 percentage points to below 50% during neoadjuvant treatment; symptomatic LV systolic dysfunction was uncommon across the study.

evidence_records.publication_title: Pegylated Liposomal Doxorubicin and Carboplatin Compared with Paclitaxel and Carboplatin for Patients with Platinum-Sensitive Ovarian Cancer in Late Relapse
evidence_records.evidence_context: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, mapped to the related NCCP ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary-peritoneal protocol.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports carboplatin plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer.
evidence_records.limitations: The comparator was carboplatin plus paclitaxel and the trial population had platinum-sensitive recurrence. Individual suitability and all current treatment criteria remain governed by the NCCP protocol.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact component combination, dose schedule and recurrent disease setting
evidence_records.trial_population: 976 patients with platinum-sensitive relapsed or recurrent ovarian cancer more than 6 months after prior platinum and taxane treatment.
evidence_records.intervention: Carboplatin AUC 5 plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m² every 4 weeks.
evidence_records.comparator: Carboplatin AUC 5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every 3 weeks.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 11.3 months versus 9.4 months; hazard ratio 0.821.
The carboplatin and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin arm had less alopecia, hypersensitivity and sensory neuropathy, but more hand-foot syndrome, nausea and mucositis.
Final overall survival was similar between treatment groups.

evidence_records.publication_title: Phase III Trial of Carboplatin and Paclitaxel Compared with Cisplatin and Paclitaxel in Patients with Optimally Resected Stage III Ovarian Cancer: a Gynecologic Oncology Group Study
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line treatment after optimal cytoreductive surgery for stage III ovarian cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 792 eligible patients with stage III ovarian cancer and no residual tumour mass greater than 1 cm after surgery.
evidence_records.intervention: Carboplatin AUC 7.5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² over 3 hours.
evidence_records.comparator: Cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus paclitaxel 135 mg/m² over 24 hours.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Progression and survival comparison within a non-inferiority design.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports carboplatin plus 3-hour paclitaxel as an effective and more practical platinum-taxane backbone in advanced ovarian cancer.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 20.7 months with carboplatin/paclitaxel versus 19.4 months with cisplatin/paclitaxel.
Median overall survival was 57.4 versus 48.7 months; gastrointestinal, renal and metabolic toxicity were less frequent with carboplatin, while thrombocytopenia was more frequent.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial population was optimally resected stage III ovarian cancer and used carboplatin AUC 7.5. NCCP 00303 spans several ovarian, peritoneal, fallopian-tube, endometrial, cervical and unknown-primary indications and an AUC range of 5–7.5; the trial is not exact evidence for every listed setting.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact drug backbone and schedule family; narrower disease population than the shared NCCP protocol
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy for Squamous Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously untreated metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 559 patients with untreated metastatic squamous NSCLC.
evidence_records.intervention: Pembrolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel for four cycles, followed by pembrolizumab.
evidence_records.comparator: Placebo plus the same chemotherapy backbone, followed by placebo.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Directly supports adding pembrolizumab to first-line carboplatin/taxane chemotherapy in metastatic squamous NSCLC.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 15.9 months with pembrolizumab combination therapy versus 11.3 months with chemotherapy alone; hazard ratio for death 0.64.
Median progression-free survival was 6.4 versus 4.8 months; hazard ratio for progression or death 0.56. Benefit was observed across PD-L1 expression categories.
evidence_records.limitations: KEYNOTE-407 permitted paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel. NCCP 00579 specifically maps pembrolizumab, paclitaxel 200 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC6, so the publication supports the strategy but includes a broader taxane choice.

evidence_records.publication_title: Sacituzumab Govitecan in Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Previously treated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 529 patients with relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer; the primary efficacy population excluded patients with brain metastases.
evidence_records.intervention: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle.
evidence_records.comparator: Single-agent chemotherapy chosen by the treating physician from protocol-specified options.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival among patients without brain metastases.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Provides direct phase 3 evidence for sacituzumab govitecan after prior systemic treatment in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months with sacituzumab govitecan versus 1.7 months with single-agent chemotherapy; hazard ratio 0.41.
Median overall survival was 12.1 versus 6.7 months, and objective response was 35% versus 5%.
evidence_records.limitations: The primary efficacy analysis excluded patients with brain metastases. The trial population was heavily pretreated and does not establish benefit in earlier treatment lines or outside triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact medicine, schedule and principal disease setting

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Trifluridine/tipiracil is an oral fixed-dose combination used for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer. The current NCCP protocol defines the treatment schedule, blood-count requirements and dose-modification pathway.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Trifluridine is the cytotoxic nucleoside component. Tipiracil inhibits thymidine phosphorylase and limits trifluridine degradation, allowing clinically useful systemic exposure.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Oral treatment on days 1–5 and 8–12 of a 28-day cycle, as specified by the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Myelosuppression is a central monitoring consideration

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab is combined with pemetrexed and carboplatin for first-line metastatic non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer without EGFR or ALK alterations.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab reduces PD-1-mediated inhibition of antitumour T-cell activity. Pemetrexed inhibits folate-dependent nucleotide synthesis, while carboplatin forms DNA cross-links. The regimen combines immune checkpoint blockade with two complementary cytotoxic mechanisms.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The NCCP protocol uses carboplatin with pemetrexed and pembrolizumab during the combination phase, followed by the protocol-defined continuation phase.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Durvalumab is used after definitive platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy in eligible patients with unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer whose disease has not progressed.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Unresectable stage III NSCLC after concurrent chemoradiotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Durvalumab blocks PD-L1 interactions with PD-1 and CD80, reducing inhibitory immune signalling and supporting antitumour T-cell activity after chemoradiotherapy.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The current NCCP regimen uses a fixed 1500 mg dose every 28 days. The original PACIFIC trial used 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks; the treatment strategy and disease setting are aligned, but the administration schedule differs.
key_points: Trial and current protocol schedules differ

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Perioperative immunotherapy with phase-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab is given with neoadjuvant carboplatin and weekly paclitaxel, followed by an anthracycline and cyclophosphamide phase, and is then continued after surgery according to the NCCP protocol.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: High-risk early or locally advanced triple-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab reduces PD-1-mediated immune inhibition. Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, carboplatin damages DNA through platinum cross-links, doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, and cyclophosphamide forms DNA cross-links after metabolic activation. The regimen combines immune checkpoint blockade with sequential cytotoxic mechanisms.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The regimen is phase based. The current opened phase and current NCCP protocol should be checked before interpreting monitoring or dose-modification rules.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Carboplatin is combined with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for platinum-sensitive relapsed or recurrent ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Carboplatin produces platinum-DNA cross-links. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin delivers doxorubicin in a long-circulating liposomal formulation; released doxorubicin intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II. The combination provides a platinum doublet without a taxane.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Carboplatin AUC 5 and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m² are administered every 28 days in the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Distinct neuropathy, hypersensitivity and hand-foot-syndrome profile

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Modified FOLFOX-6 combines oxaliplatin with folinic-acid-modulated fluorouracil. The shared NCCP protocol covers adjuvant colon cancer, metastatic colorectal cancer and advanced or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma; the exact indication should therefore be confirmed before interpreting the page.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant colon cancer; metastatic colorectal cancer; advanced or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Oxaliplatin produces platinum–DNA cross-links. Fluorouracil disrupts thymidylate synthesis and nucleic-acid function, while folinic acid stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate-synthase complex and increases fluorouracil activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: A 14-day cycle with day-1 oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion. The NCCP protocol and selected indication govern duration and dose modification.
key_points: Shared protocol with three disease contexts
DPD status is central before fluorouracil
Neuropathy assessment is central to oxaliplatin safety

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Potentially curative adjuvant therapy in selected resected colon cancer, or disease-control therapy in advanced/metastatic gastrointestinal cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the exact NCCP indication before assessment.
For fluorouracil treatment, confirm DPD status according to the current protocol and national pathway.
eligibility_orientation: Review baseline blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline peripheral neuropathy and whether it causes functional impairment.
Confirm that pregnancy, breastfeeding and relevant hypersensitivity exclusions have been addressed.
important_cautions: The MOSAIC evidence record supports the adjuvant colon-cancer setting and a FOLFOX4 schedule; it does not establish every indication in this shared modified FOLFOX-6 protocol.
Individual suitability, duration and dose decisions remain protocol- and consultant-directed.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate, mapped from the oxaliplatin-containing regimen in the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the protocol-linked moderate-risk antiemetic pathway and provide breakthrough treatment instructions.
Ensure DPD testing and fluoropyrimidine counselling are complete before first treatment.
patient_education: Explain acute cold-triggered dysaesthesia and avoidance of cold exposure after oxaliplatin.
Provide an early-contact plan for diarrhoea, stomatitis, fever, respiratory symptoms or pump/line problems.
Confirm the patient understands ambulatory infusion-pump care and the planned disconnection pathway.
special_support: Review venous-access suitability for the 46-hour fluorouracil infusion.
Escalate suspected laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia or unexplained respiratory symptoms for clinical assessment.

baseline: FBC, renal function and liver profile.
DPD status before fluorouracil exposure.
Peripheral-neuropathy assessment and relevant comorbidity review.
before_each_cycle: FBC and protocol-defined renal/hepatic review.
Current and worst-since-last-cycle diarrhoea and stomatitis.
Peripheral-neuropathy grade and persistence pattern.
Treatment delay and current component dose levels when relevant.
priority_toxicities: Oxaliplatin sensory neuropathy and acute cold-related dysaesthesia
urgent_review_signals: Fever or suspected sepsis
Persistent grade 2 or greater diarrhoea, dehydration or abdominal pain
New functional neuropathy
Chest or respiratory symptoms during or after oxaliplatin
Pump failure, extravasation or central-line complication

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 14 days: day-1 oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours in the encoded protocol.
route_and_duration: Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are administered intravenously on day 1.
Fluorouracil includes an intravenous bolus and a continuous 46-hour infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm central or otherwise locally approved venous access and ambulatory-pump arrangements.
Document the exact indication because the shared protocol covers different treatment intents and durations.
Use the official NCCP protocol for sequence, compatibility, infusion duration and dose levels.
observation_and_access: Follow local observation and hypersensitivity procedures for oxaliplatin.
Ensure a documented pump-disconnection and out-of-hours contact plan.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Intensive multiagent chemotherapy for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Modified FOLFIRINOX combines oxaliplatin, irinotecan, folinic acid and infusional fluorouracil. The NCCP protocol covers adjuvant treatment after pancreatic-cancer resection and treatment of metastatic pancreatic cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma or metastatic pancreatic cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Oxaliplatin causes platinum–DNA cross-links; irinotecan inhibits topoisomerase I through its active metabolite; fluorouracil disrupts nucleotide synthesis; folinic acid enhances fluorouracil-mediated thymidylate-synthase inhibition. The combination attacks DNA synthesis and repair through complementary mechanisms.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: A 14-day cycle with day-1 intravenous components followed by fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours. The current NCCP protocol describes treatment for up to 12 cycles and contains separate toxicity-driven component reductions.
key_points: Adjuvant and metastatic contexts share one protocol
DPD, diarrhoea and neuropathy pathways are central

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Potentially curative adjuvant therapy after resection, or disease-control therapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm whether the patient is being treated in the adjuvant or metastatic setting.
The pivotal PRODIGE 24 evidence applies to selected patients after complete macroscopic resection; metastatic use has a separate evidence base.
eligibility_orientation: Confirm DPD status before fluorouracil.
Review blood counts, renal function, bilirubin and hepatic function.
Assess for chronic bowel disease, bowel obstruction, relevant hypersensitivity, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
Assess baseline functional status and ability to manage an intensive multiagent regimen; the current NCCP protocol and consultant decision remain authoritative.
important_cautions: The regimen has overlapping gastrointestinal, haematological and neurological toxicity.
The stored primary evidence record supports the adjuvant context and should not be presented as exact evidence for metastatic treatment.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate under the current NCCP component-based classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the linked moderate-risk antiemetic pathway and a clear breakthrough plan.
Provide rapid-access antidiarrhoeal guidance and hydration advice.
Atropine may be required for acute irinotecan cholinergic syndrome according to the protocol and clinical context.
Consider protocol-directed G-CSF support after relevant neutropenic events or where clinically indicated.
patient_education: Contact the service early for diarrhoea, fever, reduced intake, dizziness or dehydration.
Explain oxaliplatin cold sensitivity and persistent-neuropathy reporting.
Explain ambulatory pump care, disconnection and line-problem escalation.
special_support: Review nutritional status and pancreatic-cancer symptom burden.
Ensure rescue medicines and written instructions are available before discharge.

baseline: FBC, renal function, bilirubin and liver profile.
DPD status.
Bowel history, neuropathy and treatment-fitness review.
before_each_cycle: FBC and protocol-defined renal/hepatic review.
Current and worst diarrhoea, stomatitis and hand-foot symptoms.
Oxaliplatin-neuropathy pattern and recurrence count.
Previous febrile/prolonged neutropenia and thrombocytopenia events.
priority_toxicities: Irinotecan acute cholinergic syndrome and delayed diarrhoea
Fluorouracil mucositis, diarrhoea and hand-foot syndrome
Hepatic and renal impairment affecting component suitability
urgent_review_signals: Fever or suspected neutropenic sepsis
Grade 2 or greater diarrhoea, dehydration or inability to maintain intake
Severe abdominal pain or possible obstruction
New functional neuropathy or persistent grade 3 symptoms
Acute cholinergic symptoms during irinotecan infusion

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 14 days with day-1 oxaliplatin, folinic acid and irinotecan, followed by fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² as a 46-hour continuous infusion in the encoded protocol.
route_and_duration: All cytotoxic components are administered intravenously.
The fluorouracil component requires an ambulatory 46-hour infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm venous access, infusion-pump supply and disconnection arrangements.
Track component-specific dose levels because toxicity may require different modifications for irinotecan, oxaliplatin and fluorouracil.
Use the official protocol for exact sequence, infusion times and compatibility.
observation_and_access: Observe for irinotecan cholinergic symptoms and infusion reactions.
Provide a documented out-of-hours pathway for diarrhoea, fever and pump complications.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Neoadjuvant dual-HER2 blockade with platinum-taxane chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: TCHP combines pertuzumab and trastuzumab with docetaxel and carboplatin for neoadjuvant treatment of HER2-positive locally advanced, inflammatory or high-risk early breast cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Neoadjuvant HER2-positive locally advanced, inflammatory or high-risk early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pertuzumab and trastuzumab bind different HER2 extracellular domains, providing complementary HER2 blockade. Docetaxel stabilises microtubules and carboplatin causes DNA cross-links. The regimen combines targeted HER2 inhibition with two cytotoxic mechanisms.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Six 21-day cycles. The encoded sequence is pertuzumab, trastuzumab, docetaxel and carboplatin on day 1, with loading doses for the first antibody cycle and maintenance doses thereafter.
key_points: Cardiac, marrow and renal monitoring are central

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Curative-intent neoadjuvant systemic therapy before definitive surgery.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm HER2-positive disease and the NCCP high-risk neoadjuvant indication.
Coordinate systemic treatment with the breast multidisciplinary, surgical and subsequent HER2-treatment plan.
eligibility_orientation: Pretreatment LVEF should meet the protocol requirement; the encoded baseline eligibility value is 55%.
Review clinically significant cardiac disease, active infection and relevant hypersensitivity.
Assess baseline peripheral neuropathy; grade 2 or greater is excluded in the encoded pathway.
Review FBC, GFR and liver profile, including bilirubin and transaminase/alkaline-phosphatase pattern.
important_cautions: TRYPHAENA was a phase 2 cardiac-safety study and not a definitive comparative efficacy trial.
Cardiac suitability and subsequent HER2-directed therapy require protocol and specialist review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High in the current SACTCheck mapping for the carboplatin-containing TCHP protocol; oncology-pharmacy validation of the local antiemetic pathway remains recorded as pending.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the protocol-linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Administer docetaxel steroid premedication according to the current protocol and local prescription pathway.
Select and document the protocol-defined dose-reduction or G-CSF strategy for haematological toxicity.
Follow local infusion-reaction prevention and management procedures for the HER2 antibodies and taxane.
patient_education: Report fever, diarrhoea, mucositis, rash, breathlessness, oedema or reduced exercise tolerance.
Explain taxane neuropathy and nail/skin symptoms.
Provide clear advice on when to seek urgent assessment after treatment.
special_support: Coordinate cardiac monitoring appointments with treatment cycles.
Ensure HER2-antibody loading status is correctly identified after delays or treatment interruptions.

baseline: FBC, GFR, liver profile and LVEF.
Neuropathy, infection, cardiac-history and hypersensitivity review.
before_each_cycle: FBC and protocol-defined count recovery.
Renal function for carboplatin dosing.
Liver profile for docetaxel suitability.
Neuropathy, stomatitis, infection and hypersensitivity assessment.
LVEF at protocol-defined intervals and whenever cardiac symptoms arise.
urgent_review_signals: Fever or suspected sepsis
New dyspnoea, oedema, orthopnoea or symptomatic heart failure
Severe infusion reaction or anaphylaxis
Marked renal decline affecting carboplatin dosing
Persistent grade greater than 2 neuropathy

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 every 21 days for six cycles: pertuzumab, trastuzumab, docetaxel and carboplatin in the encoded order.
route_and_duration: All four components are administered by intravenous infusion in this NCCP protocol.
Pertuzumab and trastuzumab use loading doses in cycle 1 and maintenance doses in cycles 2–6.
practical_workflow: Confirm antibody loading status, current docetaxel dose level and carboplatin GFR-based dose before preparation.
Use the official protocol for infusion durations, observation periods and management after delayed doses.
Coordinate surgery and post-neoadjuvant HER2 therapy outside this regimen page.
observation_and_access: Follow protocol-specific first-dose and subsequent-dose observation requirements.
Use suitable venous access and monitor closely for hypersensitivity during taxane/platinum administration.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Time-limited adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition added to endocrine therapy
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Abemaciclib is added to adjuvant endocrine therapy for eligible HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. The endocrine partner and ovarian-suppression requirements depend on menopausal status and the individual treatment plan.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant high-risk HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6, reducing retinoblastoma-protein phosphorylation and cell-cycle progression from G1 to S phase. Endocrine therapy suppresses oestrogen-receptor signalling; together they target proliferative and hormonal drivers.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Continuous oral abemaciclib with concurrent endocrine therapy for the protocol-defined adjuvant duration. Dose interruptions and stepwise reductions are used for toxicity.
key_points: Oral targeted therapy plus endocrine treatment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Curative-intent adjuvant risk reduction after definitive local treatment.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm HR-positive, HER2-negative, node-positive early breast cancer meeting the current NCCP high-risk criteria.
Confirm the intended endocrine partner and whether ovarian suppression is required.
eligibility_orientation: Review baseline FBC, liver profile, renal function and medication interactions.
Assess bowel history and ability to follow an early diarrhoea-management plan.
Review VTE risk and respiratory symptoms before and during treatment.
important_cautions: monarchE eligibility definitions and regulatory wording have evolved; current NCCP criteria are authoritative.
The treatment is additive to, not a replacement for, the appropriate endocrine regimen.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Oral moderate-high classification in the current NCCP antiemetic mapping; routine scheduled antiemetic premedication is usually unnecessary.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Provide rescue antiemetic medication when clinically indicated.
Supply a proactive diarrhoea plan with rapid access to loperamide according to local policy.
Review interacting medicines and reinforce oral-SACT adherence and missed-dose instructions.
patient_education: Contact the service at the first loose stool and maintain hydration.
Report fever, bruising, jaundice, dark urine, new cough or breathlessness, unilateral swelling or chest pain.
Explain that tablets should not be doubled after a missed or vomited dose.
special_support: Coordinate endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression where applicable and bone-health care.
Use the established oral-SACT dispensing, monitoring and contact pathway.

baseline: FBC including ANC, platelets and haemoglobin.
Liver profile and renal-function category.
Medication-interaction, VTE-risk and respiratory-symptom review.
urgent_review_signals: Persistent or recurrent grade 2 diarrhoea or any grade 3–4 diarrhoea
Fever with neutropenia or suspected infection
Jaundice or clinically significant hepatic symptoms
New unexplained cough, hypoxia or breathlessness
Symptoms suggestive of VTE
before_each_cycle: FBC and liver profile at the frequency specified by the current protocol.
Diarrhoea grade, hydration and response to supportive treatment.
Adherence, drug interactions and endocrine-treatment continuity.
Symptoms of VTE or interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Continuous twice-daily oral abemaciclib with concurrent adjuvant endocrine therapy for the protocol-defined duration.
route_and_duration: Oral administration; the endocrine partner may be oral and/or include injectable ovarian suppression.
Dose interruption and dose-level reduction are used rather than cycle-based intravenous delays.
practical_workflow: Confirm current dose level, tablet supply, adherence and interacting medicines at each review.
Document the endocrine partner and ovarian-suppression plan.
Use the official protocol for monitoring frequency, dose-reduction steps and restart criteria.
observation_and_access: No infusion access is required.
Ensure rapid telephone access for diarrhoea, fever and respiratory or thrombotic symptoms.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line immune-checkpoint and anti-VEGF combination for advanced HCC
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab combines PD-L1 blockade with VEGF inhibition for adults with advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma who have not received prior systemic therapy.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line advanced or unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Atezolizumab blocks PD-L1-mediated immune inhibition. Bevacizumab neutralises VEGF, reducing tumour angiogenesis and modifying the tumour microenvironment. The combination is intended to enhance antitumour immunity while suppressing VEGF-driven vascular support.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: A 21-day cycle with atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously or 1875 mg subcutaneously, followed by bevacizumab 15 mg/kg intravenously in the encoded protocol.
key_points: Variceal and bleeding-risk assessment before bevacizumab

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging systemic treatment for advanced or unresectable HCC.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm HCC diagnosis, advanced/unresectable status and no previous systemic therapy.
The encoded pathway requires Child–Pugh A and completion/review of oesophageal-varices screening before bevacizumab.
eligibility_orientation: Assess bleeding risk, varices, blood pressure, urine protein, recent surgery and wound healing.
Review active infection, liver function and baseline immune-related organ symptoms.
Address pregnancy, breastfeeding and relevant hypersensitivity exclusions.
important_cautions: IMbrave150 enrolled a selected population with preserved liver function and controlled bleeding risk; trial results should not be extrapolated uncritically beyond that population.
Hepatology input and local variceal-management pathways remain important.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Minimal under the current NCCP parenteral antiemetic classification; routine prophylaxis is generally not required.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Complete and act on oesophageal-varices assessment before bevacizumab.
Optimise blood pressure and address clinically significant proteinuria or bleeding risk.
Provide immune-toxicity education and a direct contact pathway.
patient_education: Report haematemesis, melaena, other significant bleeding, severe headache or neurological symptoms.
Report new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, jaundice, marked fatigue, polyuria/polydipsia or endocrine symptoms.
Discuss wound-healing and planned-procedure precautions.
special_support: Coordinate hepatology, endoscopy and antihypertensive management where required.
Ensure immune-toxicity alert information is available to the patient and other healthcare services.

baseline: Child–Pugh class and liver profile.
Oesophageal-varices screening and bleeding-risk review.
Blood pressure and urine-protein assessment.
FBC, renal function, thyroid function and other immunotherapy baseline tests according to the protocol and symptoms.
before_each_cycle: Blood pressure, urine protein and bleeding/wound-healing review for bevacizumab.
Liver profile and immune-hepatitis assessment.
Clinical screening for pneumonitis, colitis, endocrine, dermatological, renal, cardiac, neurological and other immune toxicities.
FBC and infection review when clinically relevant.
priority_toxicities: Hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding, arterial events and impaired wound healing from bevacizumab
Immune endocrine dysfunction including thyroid, adrenal and diabetic presentations
Immune cardiac, renal, neurological and severe cutaneous toxicity
urgent_review_signals: Gastrointestinal or other clinically significant bleeding
Severe or uncontrolled hypertension, neurological symptoms or arterial event
New hypoxia, chest pain, myocarditis symptoms or serious neurological syndrome
Jaundice or marked transaminase/bilirubin change
Severe diarrhoea, suspected adrenal crisis, diabetic ketoacidosis or severe cutaneous reaction

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 21 days: atezolizumab first, followed by bevacizumab in the encoded protocol.
route_and_duration: Atezolizumab may be administered intravenously or subcutaneously according to the selected protocol route.
Bevacizumab is administered by intravenous infusion at 15 mg/kg.
practical_workflow: Confirm route, variceal-screen status, blood pressure, urine protein and bleeding/wound status before release.
Use the official protocol for infusion/injection duration, observation, route-switching and delayed-dose rules.
Do not merge immune-toxicity decisions with bevacizumab-specific hold criteria; each component requires separate assessment.
observation_and_access: Follow route-specific atezolizumab observation guidance and bevacizumab infusion-reaction procedures.
Maintain immediate access to emergency assessment for bleeding or severe immune toxicity.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: FOLFIRI combines irinotecan with folinic-acid-modulated fluorouracil. The shared NCCP protocol covers advanced colorectal cancer, metastatic oesophageal carcinoma and second-line locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic carcinoma; the indication must therefore be confirmed before interpreting the evidence and treatment plan.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced colorectal cancer; metastatic oesophageal cancer; second-line locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Irinotecan is converted to SN-38, which inhibits topoisomerase I and disrupts DNA replication. Fluorouracil impairs thymidylate synthesis and nucleic-acid function; folinic acid stabilises the fluorouracil–thymidylate-synthase complex.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 14 days: irinotecan and folinic acid on day 1, fluorouracil bolus followed by a 46-hour continuous infusion, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity under the current NCCP protocol.
key_points: Shared protocol with three disease contexts
DPD status is required before fluorouracil
Delayed diarrhoea and acute cholinergic symptoms require distinct management

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging systemic therapy in advanced or metastatic gastrointestinal cancer.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm which NCCP indication applies before treatment.
The pivotal evidence record supports the metastatic colorectal-cancer backbone and does not validate every listed indication.
Confirm DPD testing before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously completed.
eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status, blood counts, renal and hepatic function.
Assess baseline bowel frequency, chronic bowel disease, obstruction risk and ability to manage diarrhoea.
Review bilirubin and hepatic reserve because irinotecan exposure and toxicity may increase with impairment.
important_cautions: Use caution in patients with more than three loose bowel movements daily, prior pelvic/abdominal radiotherapy, older age or significant comorbidity.
UGT1A1*28 homozygosity may increase irinotecan toxicity risk; testing and starting-dose decisions remain consultant-directed.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate, driven by irinotecan in the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the protocol-linked moderate-risk antiemetic pathway.
Have atropine available for acute irinotecan cholinergic syndrome when clinically indicated.
Provide a written delayed-diarrhoea treatment and escalation plan before discharge.
patient_education: Explain the difference between acute infusion-associated cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea.
Contact the service urgently for fever, persistent diarrhoea, reduced intake, dizziness or dehydration.
Explain ambulatory pump care, disconnection and line-problem escalation.
special_support: Review hydration, electrolytes and nutritional status after significant diarrhoea.
Consider oral cryotherapy/ice chips during fluorouracil bolus where locally used and not contraindicated.

DPD phenotype and/or genotype assessment according to the current pathway.
Bowel history, cardiac history where relevant and treatment-fitness assessment.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile.
Current and worst diarrhoea, mucositis/stomatitis and infection symptoms.
Recovery of treatment-related toxicity to the protocol-defined level before irinotecan.

Persistent diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dehydration or inability to maintain intake
Chest pain or acute cardiopulmonary symptoms during fluoropyrimidine exposure

Pump failure, extravasation or line complication

route_and_duration: Irinotecan is infused intravenously, followed by folinic acid/fluorouracil according to the official sequence.
Fluorouracil includes a bolus and a continuous ambulatory infusion.
practical_workflow: Confirm indication, DPD result, bowel-toxicity history and current component dose levels.
Ensure venous access, pump availability and disconnection arrangements.
Use the official NCCP protocol for exact sequence, diluents, compatibility and dose-reduction levels.
observation_and_access: Observe for acute cholinergic symptoms and infusion reactions.
Provide direct out-of-hours access for diarrhoea, fever and pump or line complications.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Platinum-taxane backbone across gynaecological cancer indications
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Carboplatin plus paclitaxel is a widely used 21-day platinum-taxane regimen. NCCP 00303 covers several ovarian, fallopian-tube, primary-peritoneal, endometrial, cervical and unknown-primary indications, so treatment intent, target AUC and duration must be confirmed for the individual indication.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Adjuvant high-risk stage I ovarian cancer; advanced ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; selected endometrial, cervical and unknown-primary settings
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules and prevents normal mitotic spindle function. Carboplatin forms platinum–DNA cross-links; AUC-based dosing links exposure to renal clearance.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² over 3 hours followed by carboplatin AUC 5–7.5 over 30 minutes on day 1 every 21 days, generally for six cycles or until progression/unacceptable toxicity depending on the indication.
key_points: Carboplatin dose depends on reliable GFR assessment
Paclitaxel premedication and hypersensitivity readiness are required
Neuropathy and cumulative marrow toxicity guide treatment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Potentially curative adjuvant treatment in selected early-stage disease, or disease-control therapy in advanced/recurrent disease.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm the exact gynaecological indication and planned carboplatin target AUC.
The GOG-158 evidence record is strongest for optimally resected stage III ovarian cancer and should not be treated as exact evidence for every protocol indication.
eligibility_orientation: Review ECOG status using the indication-specific protocol range.
Obtain FBC, renal and liver profile and a reliable GFR/CrCl assessment; measured GFR is preferred when feasible.
Assess baseline neuropathy, hearing where indicated, hypersensitivity history and pregnancy/breastfeeding exclusions.
important_cautions: Formula-derived GFR may overestimate function in obesity, low muscle mass or very low creatinine; use the protocol’s renal-dosing safeguards.
Severe hepatic impairment is an exclusion for paclitaxel, and baseline neutrophils below the protocol threshold require review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because carboplatin AUC is at least 4; use the current high-risk antiemetic pathway.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Give protocol-directed corticosteroid, H1-antihistamine and H2-antagonist premedication before paclitaxel, subject to consultant/local policy.
Ensure immediate access to anaphylaxis treatment.
Consider analgesic support for paclitaxel-associated myalgia/arthralgia.
patient_education: Report fever, rash, breathlessness or symptoms during/after infusion.
Report new numbness, pain, weakness or functional neuropathy before each cycle.
Explain that renal-function changes can alter the calculated carboplatin dose.
special_support: Review falls risk and function when neuropathy develops.
Coordinate audiometry and renal measurement when clinically indicated.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile.
Measured GFR where feasible or protocol-approved GFR/CrCl estimation.
Peripheral-neuropathy assessment and audiometry when clinically indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC with differential, renal and liver profile.
Current neuropathy grade and functional effect.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line chemo-immunotherapy for metastatic squamous NSCLC
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel and carboplatin combines PD-1 blockade with a platinum-taxane cytotoxic backbone for first-line metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1-mediated immune inhibition. Paclitaxel disrupts microtubule function and mitosis, while carboplatin forms DNA cross-links. Cytotoxic tumour-cell killing and immune activation provide complementary antitumour effects.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab 200 mg, paclitaxel 200 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC6 for four cycles, followed by pembrolizumab every 21 days until progression, unacceptable toxicity or the protocol-defined treatment limit.
key_points: Four induction cycles then pembrolizumab maintenance
High emetogenic risk from carboplatin AUC6

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging first-line systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm histological or cytological stage IV squamous NSCLC.
Review molecular/pathological context and previous anti-PD-1/PD-L1 exposure according to the current protocol and treatment pathway.
KEYNOTE-407 demonstrated benefit across PD-L1 expression categories, but individual reimbursement and protocol criteria remain authoritative.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, renal and hepatic function in the current protocol.
Review autoimmune disease, immunosuppression, unstable CNS metastases and prior severe immune toxicity.
Assess reliable GFR/CrCl for carboplatin and baseline neuropathy for paclitaxel.
important_cautions: Toxicity can arise from chemotherapy, immune activation or both; the mechanism should be considered before treatment decisions.
Paclitaxel- and carboplatin-related dose reductions do not automatically imply pembrolizumab dose reduction.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because carboplatin AUC6 is classified as high risk; pembrolizumab is minimal and paclitaxel low.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Give protocol-directed paclitaxel corticosteroid, H1 and H2 premedication.
Provide immune-toxicity education and an alert/contact pathway.
patient_education: Report fever, infusion symptoms and new neuropathy.
Report new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, jaundice, endocrine symptoms, polyuria/polydipsia or marked fatigue promptly.
Explain that immune adverse events can occur during maintenance and after treatment ends.
special_support: Review smoking-related cardiopulmonary comorbidity and baseline oxygenation when clinically relevant.
Coordinate endocrinology, respiratory or other specialty review for suspected immune toxicity.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile and a protocol-appropriate GFR assessment.
Glucose, thyroid function and hepatitis screening.
Neuropathy, hearing and autoimmune/immune-toxicity baseline assessment as indicated.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile and glucose.
Thyroid function at the protocol-defined interval.
Screen for pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrine, renal, neurological, cardiac and cutaneous immune toxicity.
Assess neuropathy, cytopenias, hypersensitivity and current chemotherapy dose levels during induction.
priority_toxicities: Immune endocrine, renal, cardiac, neurological and severe cutaneous toxicity
urgent_review_signals: New hypoxia, breathlessness or chest pain
Fever or suspected sepsis
Severe diarrhoea, jaundice or marked biochemical change
Adrenal-crisis, diabetic-ketoacidosis or severe neurological features
Acute infusion reaction or anaphylaxis

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Every 21 days: pembrolizumab first, then paclitaxel and carboplatin for cycles 1–4; pembrolizumab continues as maintenance.
route_and_duration: Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously over 30 minutes.
Paclitaxel 200 mg/m² intravenously over 3 hours using non-PVC equipment and an in-line filter.
Carboplatin AUC6 intravenously over approximately 30 minutes, with the protocol dose cap.
practical_workflow: Confirm whether the patient is in induction or maintenance.
During induction, verify paclitaxel premedication, GFR method and current cytotoxic dose levels.
Assess immune and cytotoxic domains separately and use the official protocol for component-specific holds.
observation_and_access: Follow local observation procedures for pembrolizumab and paclitaxel hypersensitivity.
Maintain urgent access for severe immune toxicity, infection or infusion reaction.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Trop-2-directed antibody–drug conjugate for previously treated metastatic TNBC
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Sacituzumab govitecan is a Trop-2-directed antibody–drug conjugate carrying SN-38. NCCP 00794 uses it as monotherapy for adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: The antibody targets Trop-2 and delivers SN-38, a topoisomerase-I inhibitor, to tumour cells. Intracellular and local payload release causes replication-associated DNA damage, creating both targeted delivery and potential bystander activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Neutropenia, diarrhoea and infusion reactions are central

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging treatment after prior systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm histologically documented triple-negative disease and the required prior systemic-therapy history.
ASCENT provides direct evidence in heavily pretreated metastatic TNBC; its primary efficacy population excluded patients with brain metastases.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–1 and adequate haematological, renal and liver function in the current protocol.
Review active infection, prior severe neutropenia/diarrhoea and capacity to attend day-1/day-8 treatment.
Address pregnancy/breastfeeding and hypersensitivity exclusions.
important_cautions: UGT1A1*28 homozygosity may increase SN-38 exposure and toxicity; the protocol advises considering a lower starting dose with possible escalation according to cycle-1 tolerance.
Dose reductions for adverse reactions should not be re-escalated.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High under the current NCCP antiemetic classification.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Give protocol-directed antipyretic, H1/H2 blockade and corticosteroid premedication as applicable for infusion-reaction prevention.
Use G-CSF according to the protocol’s severe-neutropenia occurrence pathway and local policy.
Provide immediate-access antidiarrhoeal therapy and hydration instructions.
patient_education: Report fever, diarrhoea, vomiting or reduced oral intake early.
Report flushing, rash, wheeze, swelling, dizziness or other infusion symptoms immediately.
Explain day-1/day-8 scheduling and the need for blood-count recovery before treatment.
special_support: Monitor and replace electrolytes when gastrointestinal losses occur.
Consider UGT1A1-related risk when toxicity is disproportionate or known genotype information is available.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile.
Glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, calcium and phosphate.
ECG and pregnancy testing when clinically indicated.
Baseline diarrhoea, infection and treatment-fitness review.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile before treatment.
Glucose/electrolytes and mineral profile at the protocol-defined interval.
Neutropenia/febrile-neutropenia occurrence count, diarrhoea grade and infusion-reaction history.
Confirm current dose level; do not re-escalate after toxicity reduction.
urgent_review_signals: Fever, rigors or suspected neutropenic sepsis
Persistent diarrhoea, dehydration or inability to maintain intake
Acute infusion reaction, bronchospasm or hypotension
Severe abdominal symptoms or rapid clinical deterioration
Clinically significant electrolyte disturbance or arrhythmia symptoms

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle at 10 mg/kg, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
route_and_duration: Intravenous infusion; the initial dose is delivered over 3 hours.
Observe during every infusion and for at least 30 minutes afterwards; later infusion duration follows the official protocol and tolerance.
practical_workflow: Confirm day number, weight-based dose, FBC, diarrhoea status, infection status and current dose level.
Complete antiemetic and infusion-reaction premedication before release.
Keep resuscitation treatment immediately available and use the protocol occurrence-based neutropenia/diarrhoea reductions.
observation_and_access: Continuous clinical observation during infusion and at least 30 minutes post-infusion.
Ensure rapid access for delayed fever, diarrhoea or hypersensitivity symptoms.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line chemo-immunotherapy for advanced biliary tract cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Durvalumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin combines PD-L1 blockade with a platinum–antimetabolite backbone for first-line unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer, followed by durvalumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Durvalumab blocks PD-L1-mediated immune inhibition. Cisplatin produces DNA cross-links, while gemcitabine is incorporated into DNA and inhibits nucleotide synthesis. Cytotoxic tumour injury and immune checkpoint blockade provide complementary activity.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cycles 1–8 are 21 days: durvalumab on day 1 and gemcitabine/cisplatin on days 1 and 8. From cycle 9, durvalumab continues every 28 days until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
key_points: Induction chemotherapy plus durvalumab followed by maintenance
Cisplatin hydration, electrolyte and renal safeguards
Biliary infection and immune toxicity require separate assessment

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Disease-control and survival-prolonging first-line systemic therapy.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease.
The official PDF lists PD-L1 testing among baseline tests; interpretation and reimbursement relevance should follow the current national pathway.
The TOPAZ-1 evidence record maps directly to the treatment strategy.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–2 and adequate haematological, hepatic and renal function in the current protocol.
Assess cisplatin suitability, creatinine clearance, hearing and neuropathy.
Review autoimmune disease, immunosuppression, infection, biliary stents/drains and prior severe immune toxicity.
important_cautions: Patients with biliary obstruction or stents may be at increased risk of cholangitis; fever and cholestatic deterioration need urgent source assessment, not automatic attribution to immune toxicity.
The current official PDF is version 3 but its stated review date has passed; verify the live NCCP listing before relying on version status.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High because the regimen contains cisplatin; use the current high-risk antiemetic pathway.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Provide protocol-directed pre/post hydration and magnesium with potassium when indicated for cisplatin.
Use the linked high-risk antiemetic pathway.
Provide immune-toxicity education and a direct contact pathway.
patient_education: Report fever, rigors, right-upper-quadrant pain, jaundice or changes in biliary drainage urgently.
Report reduced urine output, hearing change, tinnitus, neuropathy or severe vomiting.
Report new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, rash, endocrine symptoms or marked fatigue.
special_support: Coordinate biliary drainage/stent management and infection plans with hepatobiliary teams.
Review fluid tolerance and electrolyte replacement in patients with cardiovascular or renal comorbidity.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function.
Hepatitis B/C screening and PD-L1 testing as listed by the official protocol.
Audiology and creatinine clearance when clinically indicated.
Biliary infection/obstruction and stent/drain status.
before_each_cycle: Day 1: FBC, renal and liver profile, glucose and immune-toxicity screening.
Day 8: FBC and creatinine/renal review before gemcitabine/cisplatin.
Thyroid function at the protocol-defined interval.
Assess cholangitis, obstruction, hydration, electrolyte, hearing and neuropathy symptoms.
priority_toxicities: Cisplatin nephrotoxicity, electrolyte loss, ototoxicity and neuropathy
Immune pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrine and other organ toxicities
urgent_review_signals: Fever/rigors with biliary stent, jaundice or abdominal pain
Oliguria, significant creatinine rise or severe electrolyte disturbance
New hearing loss or disabling neuropathy
New hypoxia, chest pain or serious immune-toxicity features
Severe cytopenia, bleeding or suspected sepsis

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cycles 1–8: durvalumab on day 1, then gemcitabine and cisplatin on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; cycle 9 onward: durvalumab every 28 days.
route_and_duration: Durvalumab is infused intravenously over 60 minutes.
Gemcitabine and cisplatin are administered intravenously with protocol-directed cisplatin hydration and electrolyte support.
practical_workflow: Confirm induction versus maintenance phase and day 1 versus day 8.
Before cisplatin, verify renal function, hydration suitability, electrolytes and urine output according to local policy.
Assess infection/biliary and immune-toxicity mechanisms separately before withholding or treating.
observation_and_access: Follow local infusion-reaction procedures for durvalumab and cytotoxic therapy.
Maintain urgent access for cholangitis/sepsis, renal deterioration or severe immune toxicity.
